caveats: CPU tests, build jobs, component processes and public-consumer processes are different units and must not be summed into one test count.
The SDK 21-process list includes the reused-core columns check and a static model-lowering check. Individual row scope and source are retained.
Small flow/session/public consumers have independent formula/schedule and gradient-root checks. This does not certify FC16/LH176 scale mathematics.
Scale checkpoint validation uses a serial new owner in the same process; separate small public consumers test fresh-process restore.

Scale elapsed values are unqualified complete-training costs. No inference, grad-enabled-forward, TTFT, statistical stability, CPU/mixed speedup or direct-formula parity is established by these two runs.
FC16 scale is B4/L16/d128 and has one warmup; it is not the main B8/L128 FC16 task. LH176 has no warmup and is not a 9B model.
Both use the original 18,522,046,464-byte total reservation; workspace_bytes is an independent bound, not observed total device usage. Allocator peaks exclude untracked vendor/driver memory.

The block-v2 domain remains single-NPU FP32 aligned Settle KV sum/qry with its declared local bindings. These results do not qualify recurrent/half/multiple-device/CUDA blocks or all general PDG/TimedDAG programs.
Original projection/flow failures, CPU29/9 and SDK prerequisite timeout remain distinct terminal failures. New results do not retrospectively relabel them.
Artifacts retain original path/hash identities. Reproduction uses embedded configurations/generators/argv at fixed sources and does not require old build/run directories.
